legacy_root.question: When subcouncil conclusions are aggregated by a meta-council, what information is provably lost (dissent, confidence spread, evidence provenance), and what must be forwarded to prevent the nested-councils-disagree-on-completion failure class?
legacy_root.answer: Forwarding only each subcouncil's majority COMPLETE/BLOCKED label is a non-sufficient statistic of the member profile. In the worked 3x3 example the meta-council concludes BLOCKED (child labels 1-2) while the flattened nine members are COMPLETE 5-4. Dissent (B1, C1), within-child confidence spread, and unique evidence ids are absent from the label-only payload. The minimal forwarding set that prevents this completion reversal on the same example is per_subcouncil_verdict_counts: from those counts the parent reconstructs the 5-4 flattened majority, applies one shared completion predicate, and sees that the children disagree. Averaging child labels is the failure mode named at spec:11343. SUCCESS:RES-0087 in the receipt AND a worked two-level example showing the loss plus the minimal forwarding set that fixes it

worked_two_level_example.title: label-only-fan-in reverses flattened member majority
worked_two_level_example.why_this_is_the_failure_class: Subcouncil A reports COMPLETE and B,C report BLOCKED. A parent that majority-votes those labels, or averages them, emits BLOCKED and drops the disagreement. The shared completion predicate on the member bag emits COMPLETE.

minimal_forwarding_set.why_minimal_for_this_failure_class: Child majority labels are implied by the counts, so labels need not be forwarded separately. Flattened totals without per-child breakdown restore 5-4 COMPLETE but hide which children disagreed, which is the named failure class. Member-level verdicts, confidence vectors, and evidence ids are sufficient but not necessary for the completion reversal.

claims.canonical_mechanism: Compound-majority / referendum paradox: majority of subcouncil majority-labels can reverse the majority of members. This is the nested-councils-disagree-on-completion loss.

effect_size.this_example: certain reversal (label-only BLOCKED vs flattened COMPLETE 5-4)

claims.canonical_mechanism: Linear pooling of calibrated probabilities is itself uncalibrated, so forwarding a single mean confidence per subcouncil loses calibration and sharpness even when each member is calibrated.
claims.effect_size: TR543 Theorem 2.1: any non-trivial linear pool of distinct calibrated forecasts is uncalibrated with positive probability. On EX1, subcouncil B mean confidence 0.81 hides the 0.55 vs 0.95 split.
